# streamtime_kafka (Resource)

A Kafka cluster on a fleet. Creating one deploys the cluster and waits until it is ready. Changes to its settings are saved, but a running cluster keeps its current settings until Streamtime can apply changes to running clusters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Kafka cluster on an existing fleet. Apply waits until the cluster is ready.
resource "streamtime_kafka" "orders" {
  identifier  = "orders"
  workload    = "strimzi"
  fleet       = streamtime_fleet.byok.identifier
  kafka_units = 3

  tags = {
    team = "payments"
  }

  # Component versions, values and authentication. The fields depend on the workload.
  advanced_config = jsonencode({})

  timeouts = {
    create = "60m"
    delete = "60m"
  }
}

output "bootstrap_servers" {
  value = jsondecode(streamtime_kafka.orders.spec).bootstrapServers
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `identifier` (String) Unique name of the cluster: up to 24 lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Changing it creates a new cluster.
- `kafka_units` (Number) Cluster capacity, in capacity units.
- `workload` (String) Kafka provider of the cluster, for example strimzi, cfk, redpanda, warpstream or cpansible (Confluent Platform on your own virtual machines). Changing it creates a new cluster.

### Optional

- `advanced_config` (String, Sensitive) Advanced settings, as a JSON object set with jsonencode(): component versions, values and authentication. The fields depend on workload and may include credentials. Settings Streamtime fills in are not shown as changes.
- `alert_webhook_secret` (String, Sensitive) Secret used to sign the cluster's alert webhooks. Streamtime never returns it.
- `cloud_provider` (String) Cloud the cluster runs in, used to choose a fleet.
- `fleet` (String) Identifier of the fleet to deploy the cluster on. Leave it out to let Streamtime choose a fleet with room for the cluster's capacity, tenancy mode and cloud. Changing it creates a new cluster.
- `metadata` (String) Free-form metadata, as a JSON object set with jsonencode(). Values Streamtime adds are not shown as changes.
- `optimization_goal` (String) What the cluster's sizing favours, for example throughput or latency.
- `region` (String) Region the cluster runs in, used to choose a fleet.
- `retention_days` (Number) Days messages are kept, when retention is finite.
- `retention_mode` (String) Finite or Infinite. Streamtime does not return it, so a change made outside Terraform is not shown.
- `tags` (Map of String) Tags on the cluster, as key = value. Removing the attribute keeps the current tags; set tags = {} to clear them.
- `tenancy_mode` (String) Shared, Isolated or Dedicated.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `configuration_state` (String) Whether the cluster's settings are complete: incomplete, valid or invalid.
- `generation` (Number) Version of the cluster's settings; it goes up when they change.
- `id` (String) Same as identifier. Use the identifier to import.
- `observed_generation` (Number) Version of the settings the running cluster has.
- `reconciliation_state` (String) Progress of the last change: pending, queued, running, succeeded or failed.
- `spec` (String) What Streamtime reports about the running cluster (bootstrap servers, listeners, version), as JSON. Read it with jsondecode().
- `status` (String) Health of the cluster, for example Provisioning, Healthy or Error.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by identifier.
terraform import streamtime_kafka.orders orders
```
